title: Regional tiered economics experiments (plan and model notes)
content:
Purpose:
This note captures an experiment plan, spreadsheet schema, and a set of scenarios to evaluate a regional, tiered smart-routing policy that blends spot and on-demand capacity with fallback tiers and soft‑SLA behavior. The goal is a compact model we can iterate in Sheets to derive recommended policy hyperparameters for the optimizer (e.g., max_preempt_pct, region_fallback_margin, spot_blend_target).

Background and motivation:
- Past Optimize work focused on single-dimension savings (spot vs reserved) and region-aware heuristics. We need a reproducible experiment that ties: per-region price dynamics, customer-tier SLO penalties, and graceful degradation logic (fallback tiers).
- Engineers want clear knobs to expose (and safe defaults). Product needs mapping from business objectives (unit cost target, maximum acceptable p99 latency) to routing configs.

High-level approach:
1) Build a spreadsheet that simulates request-level routing for a configurable window (N requests) across regions and capacity tiers.
2) Introduce a stochastic spot-preemption model per region (p_preempt(t) drawn from recent price volatility and historical preempt rates).
3) Define cost and penalty functions: cost_per_token(region,tier,model) + SLA_penalty(if latency > threshold) + degrade_penalty(if fallback used).
4) Run Monte Carlo scenarios (cheap: 1k–10k trials in sheet) varying spot_blend and fallback thresholds to map cost vs user quality.

Key definitions and knobs to test:
- fallback_tiers: ordered list (e.g., [spot, reserved, on-demand]) or hybrid nodes (spot_preemptable_then_reserved).
- spot_blend_target: fraction of traffic candidate to route to spot under normal conditions.
- max_preempt_pct: max acceptable ratio of preempted requests per minute before switching to safer tier.
- region_fallback_margin: extra cost allowance to prefer local region vs cheaper remote region.
- soft_SLA_lambda: scalar for converting user-visible degradation into $ penalty in objective.

Spreadsheet schema (single flat table tabs):
- Tab: params (single-row key-value)
- Tab: region_pricing (columns)
    region, tier, base_cost_per_1k_tokens, avg_latency_ms, preempt_prob_baseline, capacity_units
  Example rows:
    us-west-2, spot, 0.16, 120, 0.04, 1000
    us-west-2, reserved, 0.28, 80, 0.0, 2000
    eu-central-1, spot, 0.12, 150, 0.06, 800
    eu-central-1, on-demand, 0.34, 90, 0.0, 1500
- Tab: workload (columns)
    request_id, customer_tier, model_size, expected_tokens, preferred_region, latency_SLA_ms, kv_cache_hit_prob
  Example row:
    r1, bronze, 7B, 48, us-west-2, 250, 0.22
- Tab: simulation_events (time-series sampled or per-request)
    trial_id, request_id, chosen_region, chosen_tier, preempted_bool, observed_latency_ms, cost_usd, applied_penalty_usd
- Tab: summary_metrics
    trial_id, avg_cost_per_request, p50_latency, p95_latency, p99_latency, percent_requests_fallen_back, total_SLA_penalty, objective = avg_cost + soft_SLA_lambda * avg_penalty

Modeling assumptions (to be explicit in sheets):
- Token length distribution is empirical from product telemetry for each customer tier (we will import a sampled histogram).
- Spot preemption model: Bernoulli(p_region_tier) per request; p varies with hour-of-day and announced capacity events (we will parametrize with multipliers).
- KV cache hit reduces expected generation tokens by factor (1 - hit_reduction). Cache hit probabilities differ by customer and model.
- Latency aggregation: chosen_tier.avg_latency_ms + network_penalty(region_distance) (we approximate network_penalty in ms).
- SLA penalty function: linear after SLA threshold (penalty_per_ms_over * ms_over) scaled by customer_tier_weight. Alternative: step penalty for > x% of requests over SLA.

Scenarios to run (minimum):
A. Baseline: spot_blend_target = 0.5, max_preempt_pct = 0.1, region_fallback_margin = 0.02 (2 cents/1k token), soft_SLA_lambda = 0.5
B. Aggressive-savings: spot_blend_target = 0.8, max_preempt_pct = 0.2, observe p99 impact and degrade_penalty
C. Safety-first: spot_blend_target = 0.2, region_preference_strict (penalize cross-region > 50ms extra latency)
D. Price-shock stress: double preempt_prob in top-2 spot regions, see worst-case cost and SLA penalty
E. KV-hit sensitivity: vary kv_cache_hit_prob from 0.1 to 0.8 to measure marginal savings and its interaction with spot usage
F. Region-switch sensitivity: test region_fallback_margin from 0 to 0.1 USD/1k tokens to see tipping point where cross-region routing is chosen

What to measure (primary outputs):
- unit_cost_usd_per_1k_tokens (including incurred SLA/penalties averaged)
- fraction_of_requests_preempted and fraction_fallen_back (metrics engineers need to set internal alerts on)
- p99 latency and rate of SLA violations by customer_tier
- expected savings vs on-demand baseline and 95% CI across Monte Carlo trials

Decision heuristics we want from spreadsheet outcomes:
- If expected unit_cost_savings > X% and p99_latency increase < Y ms -> recommend increasing spot_blend_target by Z points for that customer tier.
- If fraction_preempted > threshold (configurable per tier) -> automatically reduce spot_blend_target or increase reserved fallback weight.
- If cross-region routing increases p99 above 1.2x baseline for a premium customer -> add region_affinity override (do not route).

Operational signals & rollout plan for safe A/B:
- Start with a Canary group (small customer cohort, low revenue churn risk) with detailed logging of preempt events and rollout circuit-breaker when preempt_rate spikes > 2x baseline within 5m window.
- Telemetry: per-request tags (routing_choice, preempted, latency_components, cost_estimate) forwarded to Console to populate per-route dashboards.
- Rollout stages: Canary (1%), Expanded (10%), Default (100%) with automated rollbacks if objective degrades beyond pre-set thresholds.

Implementation notes for engineers:
- The sheet will produce recommended policy params that feed into the router as JSON feature flags (spot_blend_target, max_preempt_pct, fallback_order, region_margin_usd).
- We need a small shim service to sample real preemption signals and update the preempt_prob baseline daily; use a lookback 14-day EWMA.
- Prefer conservative defaults for premium/enterprise customers; surface explicit opt-in for aggressive spot usage in account settings.

Open questions / research items:
- Which SLA penalty mapping (linear vs step) better correlates with churn? Product to consult CS for historical churn vs SLA breach analyses (ticket: INF-7128).
- Should we treat sequence-length heavy workloads (long token sessions) differently when blending to spot due to higher preempt cost?
- What is the right cadence for updating spot_preempt_prob in production (hourly vs daily)?

Next steps (concrete):
- Build the initial sheet with tabs listed above (owner: Marcus) by EOD Friday (2025-11-14).
- Import 30 days of sampled request telemetry (engineering: Diego) and price history per region (infra: Priya).
- Run baseline and Aggressive-savings scenarios and produce a short one-pager with recommended defaults for Canary (due 2025-11-24).
- Schedule 1-hour review with Eng + Product + CS to validate SLA_penalty assumptions (invitees: Aisha, Diego, Priya, Marcus).

Appendix: Quick example CSV row for simulation_events (one line per request trial):
trial_1,r1,us-west-2,spot,false,135,0.000008,0.00
Meaning: trial id, request id, region, tier, preempted, observed_latency_ms, cost_usd, penalty_usd

Notes to self: keep the sheet lightweight (no heavy formulas) — prefer helper tabs that produce sampled inputs and then use pivoting and simple aggregates. Export from sheet into Python for larger Monte Carlo if needed.

---- END ----
